<query>I keep having this thought that parts of the town and even moments in my past have just been erased from existence, like they never happened. Could entire chunks of time or space just stop being real? If so, is that why sometimes I feel like nothing holds any meaning anymore—because parts of it aren’t even there?</query>
<response>Your feelings about parts of your past "erasing" or questioning the meaning of existence may reflect a mix of existential contemplation and emotional distress. While time and space are objective realities, subjective experiences—like memory or a sense of purpose—can feel fragmented during periods of stress, trauma, or cognitive shifts. This might relate to how your mind processes identity and continuity. However, if these thoughts persist or disrupt your well-being, consider discussing them with a mental health professional. They can help explore whether this reflects temporary overwhelm, a neurological pattern, or deeper existential concerns. For now, grounding practices (e.g., journaling, connecting with others) might ease the sense of disconnection.</response>
